newsitem.title: USA: Chubb's stock soars on report it may sell units.
newsitem.headline: Chubb's stock soars on report it may sell units.

text.p: Chubb Corp.'s stock shot up 11 percent Friday after analysts said the insurance company told Wall Street analysts it was considering the possible sale of its life and real estate businesses.
Company officials were not immediately available Friday to comment on the reports about its plans, which analysts said the company revealed late Thursday in a conference call.
Chubb's stock soared $5, or about 11 percent, to $50.50, in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was one of the most active issues.
The stock had lost $3.50 Thursday after the company reported disappointing third-quarter earnings, which were hurt by catastrophe losses and slow premium growth.

Analysts said that Chubb Chief Executive Dean O'Hare told them in the conference call that the company was considering the possible sale of its life and real estate units in a move to improve shareholder value.
Decisions about how to proceed could come as early as December, Smith Barney analyst Ron Frank said.

Bear Stearns analyst Steven Gavios said Warren, N.J.-based Chubb may use the assets from the sale of those businesses to buy back shares, make acquisitions or build up the infrastructure of some of its other businesses.
The life operations currently have equity of $842 million and the real estate operations have equity of $426 million, Gavios said in a research report.
He upgraded the stock to buy from attractive and has a 12- to 18-month price target of at least $65 a share.
"We believe the sum of the parts is worth $65 a share or higher," Gavios told Reuters.

"We believe that Mr. O'Hare's patience has run out, with the turnaround at the life operations happening slower than expected, which pushed out the waiting time until the earnings performance would be up to par," Gavios said in his report.

"Additionally, with the dramatic consolidation of the life insurance industry going on today, Chubb has come to the realisation that being a player in the life business would have required it to double down on its investment, which management did not think was prudent," Gavios said.

"Mr. O'Hare tells us that the company is well into the process of evaluating its alternatives and that it should make meaningful headway on the decision process by year-end," Gavios said in the report.
Chubb said Thursday that its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 fell to $165.2 million, or 93 cents a share, from $171.4 million, or 97 cents a share.
